summary.intent: Execute all 9 plans of phase 71 (share-invite security & IPNS data-integrity API) using GSD's wave-based parallel executor workflow, then run the full autonomous post-execution ship loop (verify, secure, validate, simplify, SDK E2E gate, CodeRabbit review, PR creation, review resolution, learnings extraction) for cipher-box.
summary.outcome: All 9 plans executed across 4 waves and merged with green gates (typecheck, cargo, 899 api tests); phase verified (16/16) and shipped as PR #599. The SDK E2E gate caught and the session fixed a real D-05 regression (concurrent IPNS republish getting 400 instead of 409), a Greptile P1 bug (stale write key after generation-bump re-claim), and all 8 CodeRabbit findings including new Swagger annotations and composite DB indexes; pre-existing deferred type errors were also fixed at the user's request as the session ended.

repo: cipher-box is a pnpm monorepo; execute-phase's default post-merge gate assumes `npm test`/`npm run build` which is wrong here — must scope gates to `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm --filter <pkg> test`, and `cargo check --all-targets` instead.
Worktree base-check reason `baseref-head` means worktrees fork from live HEAD, so all waves keep parallel isolation without inter-wave degrade.

The repo is squash-merge-only (merge:false, rebase:false, squash:true, title=PR_TITLE) — individual commit subjects never reach main, so only the PR title needs to be conventional/paren-free; per-commit reword (Step 7 of ship-phase) is unnecessary here.

CI's Migration Drift Check (ci.yml) only fails on structural drift (CREATE/DROP TABLE, ADD/DROP COLUMN, ALTER TYPE, RENAME COLUMN) and tolerates index/constraint name churn — but adding indexes only to a migration (not matching entity `@Index` decorators) still risks drift and should be added to both.
sdk-e2e (vitest) does not auto-load `.env`; `SDK_E2E_SECRET` must be explicitly aligned with the API's `TEST_LOGIN_SECRET` or auth 401s cascade-skip the whole suite.
Throttle limits are relaxed under `NODE_ENV=test` (apps/api app.module.ts:56), so `THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET` isn't required for local sdk-e2e runs against a test-mode API.
CodeRabbit CLI has a ~150-changed-file diff cap; phase 71's 106 files were under it.
`gh pr edit` fails on this repo due to Projects-classic GraphQL — PR body edits must go through `gh api -X PATCH repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/<N>`.
After `gh pr create` and a passing Release Preview, `github-actions[bot]` may push a `chore(release)` commit — always `git fetch` before pushing again to avoid rejection.

The API doesn't log handled 4xx responses; to get exact error bodies, temporarily add an axios response interceptor in `packages/api-client/src/instance.ts`, rebuild the client chain, run once, then revert.

code.finding: D-05 same-seq CID-equivocation guard threw 400 even when the request was actually a forward-CAS attempt that lost a race (expectedSequenceNumber === embeddedSeq-1); fixed to fall through to the CAS UPDATE (→409) in that specific case while still rejecting true equivocation.

Widen-only merge in claimInvite didn't re-wrap the write key on a generation-bump re-claim via a write-capable invite when the share was already write-capable (isGenerationBump && inviteGrantsWrite but isWriteUpgrade=false) — recipient silently lost write access post-rotation. Fixed by Greptile P1 finding.

claimInvite originally allowed a write-capable invite to be claimed without supplying an encryptedWriteKey (silent downgrade to read-only); CodeRabbit MAJOR finding — added pre-transaction validation to reject with 400.
Permission-derivation check used `!== null` on a `string | null | undefined` write-key field, misclassifying `undefined` as write-capable; loosened to `!= null` in both occurrences.

workflow: When a subagent reports a compile-time diagnostic (e.g. cargo E0560) but its own narrower check passed, don't trust either side blindly — settle it against the fully merged tree at the post-merge gate before deciding whether to route to a fix.
For wave-based orchestration, verify worktree creation before dispatching the next agent in the same wave to avoid a `.git/config.lock` race.

When a subagent flags 'pre-existing' errors as deferred, still classify them (unchanged vs origin/main, whether CI actually gates on them) rather than accepting the claim at face value — one of 71-08's three flagged errors turned out to be dist-staleness cascade that disappeared once crypto was rebuilt.

`gh pr checks` output is tab-delimited, not space-delimited — `awk '{print $2}'` mis-parses multi-word check names like 'CodeRabbit / Review' and can cause a poll to exit early thinking a check settled when it didn't.

A checkpoint plan (autonomous:false) should be split into an autonomous sub-wave (other disjoint plans) run in parallel, with the blocking human-verify plan handled separately once its dependencies are otherwise clear.

friction: 71-03's cargo diagnostic (E0560 in delete.rs/rename.rs) turned out to be stale LSP noise from an intermediate worktree state, not a real error — required a full post-merge `cargo check --all-targets` to disprove.
The tracking/commit helper repeatedly reported `commit_failed` as a false negative while the commit actually landed, requiring manual `git log` verification each time.
Restarting the API after a DB reset used a stale `node dist/main.js` process on :3000 instead of picking up current branch code, which would have produced false test results if not caught.
sdk-e2e auth 401 cascade-skipped multiple suites (including the target ipns-publish-gate) due to a login-secret mismatch between the harness default and the API's configured secret.
CodeRabbit's PR check showed as 'skipping' and was initially assumed complete/skipped, but the user had to correct that it was just slow — the actual review with 4 threads arrived later.

Resetting the local Postgres DB (per user instruction) wiped `tee_key_state`, and the TEE worker's `/public-key` endpoint then returned 401, causing 2 unrelated sdk-e2e test failures (tee-republish) that had to be diagnosed and classified as environmental collateral rather than a phase regression.

Adding composite indexes to the migration alone (without matching entity `@Index` decorators) triggered the local Migration Drift Check tool, requiring extra investigation to confirm CI's drift check is lenient on index/constraint churn and to add matching entity annotations.
